title: A Conversation With Ari Emanuel About Entertainment and AI
text: A Conversation With Ari Emanuel About Entertainment and AI – Stratechery by Ben Thompson Skip to content By Ben Thompson About Email/RSS @benthompson Explore Concepts Companies Topics Menu Search × Stratechery Plus Subscribe Log In Learn More Member Forum By Ben Thompson About Email/RSS @benthompson Explore Concepts Companies Topics More by Ben Thompson Updates Interviews Year in Review All Articles Latest Podcast Netflix Angst, The End of the Internet, Q&A on Meta’s VR Glasses, Anthropic Alignment, You Can See Everything Sharp Tech | Oct 23 Netflix Angst, The End of the Internet, Q&A on Meta’s VR Glasses, Anthropic Alignment, You Can See Everything A Conversation With Ari Emanuel About Entertainment and AI Thursday, October 15, 2026 Listen to Podcast Listen to this post: Good morning, This week’s Stratechery Interview ended up not being an Interview, but rather a conversation with Hollywood super-agent Ari Emanuel . Emanuel is the Executive Chairman of WME Group , Executive Chair and CEO of TKO Group Holdings (the owner of UFC and WWE), and Founder of MARI , a live events and experiences company. The occasion for this conversation née interview was the recent publication of Emanuel’s memoir, Roll the Calls , a reference to Emanuel’s relentless daily phone call routine; I got on Emanuel’s roll for the first time a couple of years ago, and quickly learned that when Emanuel wants something he gets it. That’s a theme of his book, and of this interview: Emanuel decided he wanted to have a conversation and ask me some questions too, so that’s exactly what we did. We cover everything from the state of social networks, AI’s impact on Hollywood and the tech industry, and what skills might not just persist but become more valuable. We also discuss why Emanuel is making such a big bet on live, whether or not Hollywood is logical, and whether talking on the phone is the antidote to polarization. As a reminder, all Stratechery content, including interviews, is available as a podcast; click the link at the top of this email to add Stratechery to your podcast player. On to the conversation: A Conversation With Ari Emanuel About Entertainment and AI This interview is lightly edited for clarity and content. Topics: The State of Social | Roll the Calls | AI and Creativity | Buying UFC | Post-AI Tech | AI and Generational Change | MARI | Hollywood Logic The State of Social Ari Emanuel: Can I ask you one question? Because I saw your interview . Who was it — you did it with a guy in New York. Patrick O’Shaughnessy ? AE: Patrick, yeah, who I love. Yeah, I read your interview with him , it was great. AE: I loved your point of view, and explain a little bit more to me because I love your thinking — that on a SaaS model, the only one, based on my understanding, based on your model right now, that’s got it right, OpenAI should have gone to advertising as opposed to charging, Muse has it right. Yeah, for sure. AE: They don’t need to charge you because they have the other revenue stream. Right. And well, not just that, but the LLM, like, it’s actually really interesting. So when they launched Muse, they made this promise, “We won’t use your data that you use with Muse for advertising”, and no one cares . No one knows they made that promise, and no one cares, because no one cares about that stuff. And so they, in some respects, handicapped themselves by making this promise. AE: Just like Apple, we’re not going to look at your data, major mistake when Tim [Cook] said that. Right. But in the long run, I think it’s going to pay off, because you’re going to have this complete change in how advertising works. Right now you sort of have data on the user and you have data, broadly speaking, of what a particular product matches with and you’re matching, it’s called the two-towers approach . So you’re matching these two things together, and that’s how advertising basically works at scale, and it’s all these vector databases, all these sorts of things. AE: Television never did it properly. That’s right. So the way advertising is going to work in the future, and it’s already happening, is it’s going to predict what you want. AE: Well, the funny thing, what I thought when you said that— (laughing) I can never remember if I’ve said it before. AE: One is, Mark is going to be able to make a ton personally and charge, he’s going to be able to use the AI to do it, and it’s going to be just more and more and more. It’s more than that. So what you’re going to do is you’re going to get a personalized ad predictor that basically is inside your VM. They’re going to be credibly able to say it’s totally private, because it is totally private. AE: Because it’s just directed at you. That’s right, it’s just predicting what you want to see. Just like it’s going to be a predictor of content you want to see. AE: Oh, I didn’t think about it that way, yeah. The reason why there’s such massive upside is this whole agent thing — this is the real Google threat. So everyone thought when ChatGPT came out, that was a threat to Google, but the human was still in the loop . As long as the human is still in the loop, Google is okay. But all of Google Search, Amazon search— AE: Once the human is out of the way… Then all these search-skim ad models, which is what all these models are, they’re all bullshit models, because it’s just attacks on search. AE: Well, are you saying the same thing about Amazon? Yeah, 100%. AE: I think Amazon, because of Muse — I mean, Walmart made the deal with them. Which is a huge deal .
